clue.text: Old revolutionary in the firing line

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary

explanation.surface: A veteran rebel is facing the firing squad.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an execution; the firing line is really the mark darts players throw from.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the throwing line, where players stand to fire their darts, is called the oche.

clue.text: Gross saying about death sentences?

parts.note: gross, as in very overweight, means fat

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the word for saying is read backwards

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A crude proverb concerning capital punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that these 'sentences' are religious rulings, some of which call for a death.
explanation.definitionFit: Edicts issued by Islamic clerics, notoriously sometimes ordering a killing, can be described as death sentences.

clue.text: Excessive amount left in narrow passage

indicators.note: in says the letter for left goes inside the word for the passage

parts.note: a gut is a narrow channel or strait

explanation.surface: Too much of something has been dumped in an alley.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversupply, more than the market can absorb, is a surplus or excess.

clue.text: Service area for butcher

parts.note: Mass is a church service
an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: A motorway service area is looking for a butcher to stock its shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To butcher people is to slaughter them in large numbers, a verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: Tube station's second to none

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the words tube station have the answer within them

explanation.surface: A boast that a particular Underground stop is unbeatable.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across tuBE STation. Pete Best, the early Beatles drummer, fits the puzzle's theme of drummers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second to none is unsurpassed, the finest of all.

clue.text: Revolutionary sort of chemical treated ill son

indicators.note: sort, as a verb meaning arrange, tells us to rearrange the word chemical
treated means processed or altered, so the letters of ill son are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemical of some kind has been given to a sick boy as medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams give the two names. Michael Collins was the Irish revolutionary leader; Phil Collins is a theme drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish independence leader killed in 1922 was a famous rebel against British rule.

clue.text: Actor playing Romeo

indicators.note: playing, as in playing around, means the letters of Romeo are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer taking the role of Shakespeare's lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Moore, the James Bond star, is a well-known film actor.

clue.text: A sheep eating pasture, ultimately devoured completely

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the sheep word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of pasture

explanation.surface: A sheep grazes the field until it is all gone.
explanation.definitionFit: To have consumed every last bit of something is to have finished eating it.

clue.text: "Man on board" includes the German getting up when it's still dark

indicators.note: includes signals that the chessman holds the German word inside it

parts.note: a pawn is a chess man on the board

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the German article is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A shout warning that someone is aboard, heard as the German rises before daylight.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Man on board' look like a cry; it is a chess piece. 'getting up' fits a down clue, where reading upwards means backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours just before sunrise, when it is not yet light, are the pre-dawn period.

clue.text: Manage to cycle round a group of oil-producing countries

indicators.note: cycle round says the first letter moves round to the end

parts.note: OPEC is the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries

explanation.surface: Someone tries to bicycle around a whole bloc of oil states.
explanation.walkthrough: OPEC with its O cycled to the back gives the answer. With 20 Across it also makes Stewart Copeland, a theme drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by or deal with a situation successfully is to handle it.

clue.text: Power units in Temple tube station's vans

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia

indicators.note: vans are vanguards, the fronts, so the first letters of tube and station are taken

explanation.surface: Delivery vans at Temple Underground station need electrical power.
explanation.walkthrough: Temple is a real London Underground station, which makes the surface plausible. Charlie Watts of the Rolling Stones is a theme drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical power is measured in units named after the engineer James Watt.

clue.text: Letters of support?

definitions.meaning: the twentieth letter of the alphabet, more than once
small pegs that support a golf ball for the first stroke

explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the letter T, and also the golf pegs a ball rests on for driving.

clue.text: One who wants backing over piano being played again

indicators.note: over means covering, so the reversed word sits round the letter for piano
backing means going backwards, so the word for one who wants is reversed

parts.note: a desirer is one who wants something
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A would-be patron is asking for support for a pianist's repeat performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical theme repeated later in a work, or a role performed once more, has been given a reprise.

clue.text: Fish recipe, with fish left out

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

indicators.note: out means omitted, so the letter for left is removed from the fish

parts.note: a loach is a small freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A recipe for fish that somehow leaves the fish out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' looks like one phrase, but 'left' gives L and 'out' is the removal signal. Max Roach was a jazz drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of the carp family is a familiar coarse-angling catch.

clue.text: Kind of wheat outside upper-class house

indicators.note: outside says the word for house goes around the letter for upper-class

parts.note: drum is old slang for a house or dwelling

explanation.surface: Some grain is growing outside a grand country house.
explanation.walkthrough: DRUM for a house is British slang, not everyday use.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard wheat variety used for pasta and semolina.

clue.text: Hour on horse? A mount's heading for Surrey village

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the letter for hour follows the horse

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

indicators.note: heading means the first letter, here of mount

explanation.surface: Someone spends an hour on horseback heading to a Surrey village.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south of London. Billy Cobham is a jazz-rock drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: A village in Surrey, England, near the A3 and the river Mole.

clue.text: Wind out through this when leaving Basel, Switzerland

indicators.note: leaving says the word for when departs from Basel

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
CH is Switzerland's international code, from Confoederatio Helvetica

explanation.surface: Directions for letting off wind on the way out of Basel, Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through this' simply links: the answer comes through the wordplay that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting stomach gas escape noisily through the mouth is a burp.

clue.text: Song some gay MC announced

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cheerful master of ceremonies introduced a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1978 disco hit by the Village People, famous for its arm-spelling dance.

clue.text: Military officer, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word for officer is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a marshal is a high-ranking officer, as in field marshal

explanation.surface: An army officer, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase with 'say' meaning 'for instance'; Military is the definition and the officer is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to war or the armed forces, as in martial law.

clue.text: Scoundrel that's a Nobel Prize winner

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel
that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A villain who has nonetheless won a Nobel Prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in both physics and chemistry.

clue.text: Bach's confused with REM? Judge works here

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters of Bach's and REM are rearranged

explanation.surface: Mixing up Bach with the rock band REM, while a judge looks on.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's private rooms in court, where hearings may be held, carry this name.

clue.text: Bag lady regularly eats one

indicators.note: eats says the picked letters take in the word for one
regularly picks every other letter of lady

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A bag lady routinely consumes a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bag lady' reads as one phrase, but Bag is the definition and only lady is used for letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag something is to catch or secure it, as an angler lands a fish.

clue.text: Composer's unfinished finale to opera for Hindu god

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Brahms was a German composer

indicators.note: finale to means the final letter of opera

explanation.surface: A composer's incomplete ending to an opera about a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The creator god in the Hindu trinity alongside Vishnu and Shiva.

clue.text: Cambridge University has small room housing Hungary's top writer

parts.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is a university in Cambridge, Massachusetts

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the room word contains the letter

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison

indicators.note: top means the first letter of Hungary

explanation.surface: A college with a little room where Hungary's leading author lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge suggests England, but this is Cambridge, Massachusetts. Writers include Margaret and David Mitchell; Mitch Mitchell drummed for Hendrix.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell wrote Gone with the Wind, and David Mitchell wrote Cloud Atlas.

clue.text: Delight as farm brings in harvest — rapeseed, initially

indicators.note: brings in says the word for farm takes the letters inside

parts.note: to farm land is to till it

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of harvest and rapeseed

explanation.surface: Pleasure as a farmer gathers in the oilseed crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden feeling of excitement or pleasure; also usable as a verb, to excite.

clue.text: City in Italy, on Sardinia

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the following words

explanation.surface: A city found in Italy, on the island of Sardinia.
explanation.walkthrough: Italy suggests an Italian city; the answer is the French city, in its older English spelling with S.
explanation.definitionFit: A major city in south-east France, often spelt with a final s in English.

clue.text: Loaded rifle, in case harassment starts

indicators.note: starts picks the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A gun is kept loaded as protection against harassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' seems to describe the rifle; it means wealthy. Buddy Rich is a theme drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for very wealthy, having plenty of money.

clue.text: Feature of can-can giving drunk a 23

parts.note: high can mean intoxicated
the answer to 23 Down means delight, which a kick also means, as in 'get a kick out of it'

explanation.surface: A cancan dancer's display gives a tipsy spectator a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancers in the Parisian cancan famously fling a leg up above head height.

clue.text: Mug dropping ecstasy — one with a bun in the oven?

definitions.text: one with a bun in the oven?

indicators.note: dropping means losing, so the letter is removed from the mug word

parts.note: a beaker is a mug or drinking cup
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A fool giving up the drug, now expecting a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bun in the oven' is slang for pregnancy; here it is literal baking. Ginger Baker of Cream is a theme drummer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bakes bread and buns for a living literally puts buns in the oven.

clue.text: See 26
A day without love for Titania, perhaps

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the day goes around the letter

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday, a day
love means zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A day without love for Shakespeare's fairy queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Titania suggests A Midsummer Night's Dream, but here she is a satellite of Uranus. 'without' is the old sense, outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the largest satellite of Uranus, an example of a planet's natural satellite.

clue.text: Animal forgets intro repeatedly before performing linked set of pieces in a suit

definitions.text: linked set of pieces in a suit

indicators.note: performing, like a circus act, signals the remaining letters are rearranged
forgets intro means the first letter is dropped, and repeatedly means doing that twice

explanation.surface: A circus animal keeps forgetting its entrance and performs in costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first letter twice from Animal leaves IMAL, which 'performing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour of interlocking metal rings, worn as a protective garment by knights.

clue.text: Big cat, cross with queen after first of each litter is gone

indicators.note: after says the queen's letters follow the picked letters
first of each picks the opening letters of litter, is and gone

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A big cat is annoyed with the queen once the litter's firstborn has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring of a male lion and a female tiger, a hybrid feline.
